scope: External diff/oracle tool implementation study; no upstream tool executed.

tools.name: asm-differ

capabilities.purpose: Assembly diff viewer for matching decompilation
formats: limited parsed x86 ELF/COFF/OMF-like relocation spellings
capabilities.recompilation_feedback_loop: Optional configured make and filesystem watch
capabilities.data_layout: Display-level sections/rodata references, no full object/layout proof
capabilities.relocations: Text normalization for selected architecture relocation records
feedback: source/line display when objdump supplies it
capabilities.historical_x86: Limited x86/i686 parser includes 16-bit relocation spellings but is not an OMF/MZ/NE parser

findings.claim: Current upstream implements x86/i686 settings and an x86 relocation processor; README labels x86 support limited.
The score separates stack and likely register-allocation differences from reordering and insertion/deletion, but is a heuristic display score rather than strict equality.

tools.reuse_decision: Use as a UI/feedback-design reference or optional external viewer; do not use as strict oracle or OMF/MZ/NE proof parser.
limitations: no candidate history or output clustering

tools.name: objdiff

capabilities.purpose: Relocatable-object code/data diff and project UI
formats: relocatable objects; source uses object backend COFF and ELF relocation variants
capabilities.compiler_specific_behavior: Format/compiler accommodations such as symbol handling, no compiler forward model
capabilities.recompilation_feedback_loop: Configured base/target builds plus file watch
capabilities.data_layout: Code, data, BSS/common symbols and sections
capabilities.relocations: First-class type/target/addend records with configurable relaxation
capabilities.scoring: Typed instruction diff with weighted immediate/register/replace/insert-delete score and match percentage
capabilities.historical_x86: Promising for COFF/x86 diagnostic use; no OMF reader found

findings.claim: ObjectDiff records typed instruction, branch, data and relocation differences; code comparison can relax relocation differences by configuration.

tools.reuse_decision: Highest-value optional out-of-process adapter candidate for Icy Tower COFF/x86 diagnostics; preserve local raw identities and strict acceptance separately.
limitations: no candidate search, AI or clustering

tools.name: reccmp

capabilities.purpose: Annotated original/recompiled image comparison for decompilation projects
capabilities.known_compiler: Old MSVC knowledge through PDB/CV and matching rules, not a generic historical compiler model
capabilities.output_deduplication: Aggregate selects/combines saved accuracy reports, not equivalent compiler-output clustering
capabilities.translation_unit_context: PDB/source annotation identification, no TU construction search
capabilities.data_layout: Functions, variables, vtables, imports/exports and sections
capabilities.relocations: Image parsers include PE/NE relocation structures; not an OMF object/fixup comparator
capabilities.scoring: Accuracy/match ratio plus semantic effective-match convention
capabilities.historical_x86: Directly relevant only where the target is old 32-bit MSVC with a usable recompiled PDB

findings.claim: The comparison setup ingests a recompiled PDB through cvdump and source annotations, then matches entities; effective-match logic explicitly analyzes register/operand differences.

tools.reuse_decision: Study/use as a standalone AGPL tool only for a future compatible old-MSVC/PDB project; do not copy/link into ai_decomp and do not use effective match as strict proof.
limitations: semantic normalizations can mask strict differences

tools.name: binutils-omf
tools.license: GPL-2.0-or-later for inspected bfd/i386omf.c; repository-wide redistribution requires component audit

capabilities.purpose: GNU BFD/binutils fork with i386 OMF reading used by decomp.me for omf-nm and omf-objdump diagnostics
capabilities.languages: N/A: object inspection/disassembly, not source reconstruction
capabilities.data_layout: BFD object representation; no local proof of private-contribution or linker-topology semantics
capabilities.relocations: i386 OMF reader decodes FIXUPP/FIXUPP386 target/frame variants; raw record-order preservation was not established
capabilities.historical_x86: Directly relevant diagnostic support for old x86 OMF; no demonstrated strict OMF/NE/MZ acceptance capability

findings.claim: The i386 OMF BFD reader defines FIXUPP/FIXUPP386 and implements decoding for FIXUPP target and frame methods.

tools.reuse_decision: Evaluate only as an invoked, GPL-separated disassembly/symbol diagnostic after corpus parity tests; do not copy or link the parser into ai_decomp.
limitations: No source recovery or compile loop
raw FIXUPP record order and semantic equivalence unverified

sources.role: Pins binutils-omf v0.4 as an MS-DOS objdump/nm diagnostic
GPL-2.0-or-later i386 OMF reader with FIXUPP/FIXUPP386 decoding
